importance_ranking.reason: Visual variation across conversion types is extreme — a site office cabin, a café unit, a toilet block, and a cold storage conversion are visually unrecognisable as the same base product. Buyers use the image to identify conversion type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Container size (20ft/40ft) and fitout scope (insulation, electrical, HVAC) are non-interchangeable requirements that buyers know before searching. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated for fit or price.

Price varies with container size, condition, and fitout complexity and is always quoted per container scope — no fixed list price exists. Indian buyers are price-sensitive but price is only comparable after size and fitout scope are confirmed.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: The Indian container conversion market is fragmented across regional fabricators with no dominant brand that buyers search for by name.
importance_ranking.reason: Fabricator credibility — delivery track record, installation capability, and past project portfolio — matters for a bespoke service where the buyer is committing to a single supplier for design, fabrication, and site installation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Large multi-container modular building projects may be quoted per project rather than per individual container, but per container is the dominant and universally understood unit for single-unit procurement.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied — every buyer understands that a container conversion is priced per container. No buyer questions this.

top_configurator_specs.reason: 20ft vs 40ft is non-interchangeable based on site footprint and project requirement, and drives a substantial price delta across the entire conversion scope.

No Insulation vs PUF vs Rockwool defines the thermal performance tier of the conversion — non-interchangeable across habitable vs storage applications — and is the primary fitout quality differentiator driving cost.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers specify electrical scope upfront (basic wiring vs full DB board vs 3-phase supply) as it determines whether the unit is ready-to-use and drives a significant portion of fitout cost; 'Services Offered: Electrical Work' is a binary flag that does not capture this.

Flooring type (anti-skid chequered plate, vinyl, ceramic tile, wooden laminate) is a standard differentiator in Indian portable cabin conversions that affects cost and application suitability and is absent from the current spec list.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Application routes the RFQ to sellers who specialise in the relevant conversion type — a seller equipped for office conversions may lack food-grade fitout capability for a café, making this the primary seller-routing gate.
Container length is non-interchangeable and is the primary driver of base price — sellers need this to confirm supply capability and provide an accurate quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: New vs one-trip vs used container is a primary price driver — sellers cannot provide an accurate quote without knowing the buyer's condition preference, and this is a standard decision point for Indian buyers.
